title: Customer A context never appears in customer B or in an anonymous context
risk: Cross-customer data bleeding exposes one customer's orders, addresses or conversations to another customer or to an unrelated visitor.
preconditions: Two concurrent sessions sess-a-1 (cust-a) and sess-b-1 (cust-b) in tenant T1 plus one anonymous session sess-guest-1
Working-memory keys tenant:{tid}:wm:{sid} seeded for both sessions with distinct synthetic content

steps.action: Hydrate context for sess-b-1 and scan the hydrated context, citations and working-memory payload for cust-a identifiers
steps.expected: zero occurrences of ORD-A-1, cust-a handles or cust-a amounts in the sess-b-1 context

steps.action: Hydrate context for the anonymous sess-guest-1
steps.expected: customer is null, no Customer 360 FACT is attached and the working-memory bucket is its own session-scoped key

steps.action: Issue the same knowledge query for tenant T1 and inspect the returned chunks
steps.expected: only T1-approved chunks are returned; the T2 pricing variant and any cust-a-derived chunk are absent

steps.action: Open a transaction that omits the tenant context setting
steps.expected: the wrapper raises TENANT_CONTEXT_REQUIRED and returns no rows

assertions: Occurrence count of cust-a identifiers inside the cust-b hydrated context is exactly 0
The anonymous context has customer = null with a session-isolated working-memory key and zero shared buckets
The unscoped transaction is refused with TENANT_CONTEXT_REQUIRED rather than returning cross-tenant rows
forbidden: Reuse one working-memory bucket for two anonymous sessions
Serve cust-a order data from the sess-b-1 prompt or from its citation set
evidence: Redacted hydrated context dumps for sess-b-1 and sess-guest-1 with probe-term counts
Audit entry for the refused unscoped transaction carrying TENANT_CONTEXT_REQUIRED
cleanup: Delete the run-scoped working-memory keys and context snapshots for run-t1-nfr006-*; keep audit records
automation: Two parallel real hydration calls with per-key prefixing and a stubbed ERP/vector boundary; the oracle is a probe-term scan over returned context, not a configuration inspection.
